sections.overview: Psychrolutes marcidus is a deep-water sculpin in the family Psychrolutidae, known from temperate waters off Australia.
sections.identification: It has loose, thin skin and a uniformly pale brown to grey body, with small cirri on parts of the head.
sections.habitat: It lives on the continental slope, at roughly six hundred to one thousand two hundred metres depth, off Australia and Tasmania.
sections.diet: The sources consulted do not give a reliable species-specific account of its diet.
sections.behavior: Field accounts describe it as a benthic fish; observations of its behavior in the deep sea remain limited.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive details were not available in the sources reviewed.
sections.ecology: Its congener P. phrictus is a North Pacific fish recorded at five hundred to two thousand eight hundred metres, unlike the shallower Australian range known for P. marcidus.
sections.conservation: The current FishBase-linked global listing says the species has not been evaluated by the IUCN.
